source.title: Explorations of Self-Repair in Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The study reports qualitative evidence about backup name-mover heads in IOI, using a different analysis from the original circuit evaluation.
record.gate_note: The study also reports extensive self-repair results on general pretraining-distribution tokens. Those do not measure the IOI circuit or the other claim versions, so they are not included as rows. Its IOI discussion reports qualitative findings, without numerical results or detailed experimental conditions.
record.test_reason: Only Section 5.3.1 touches the IOI circuit. It gives one qualitative, preliminary result relevant to V2: when the residual stream read by the Name Movers is fed to the Backup Name Movers (equivalent to zero-ablating the components in between), the backup heads begin name moving. No numbers, model, prompts or sample size are given. The rest of the paper measures direct-effect self-repair on The Pile, not the IOI circuit.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right, but it omits the main conclusion. The authors' main conclusion is that self-repair of single attention heads exists across the full pretraining distribution and many models, but is imperfect and noisy. LayerNorm rescaling (about 30%) and sparse anti-erasure neurons are mechanisms behind it. As speculative support for an Iterative Inference hypothesis, they cite IOI backup name movers. They note counter-evidence: induction, previous-token and S-inhibition heads do not appear to be repaired iteratively.
record.recipe_differences: The study primarily measures direct-effect self-repair on general pretraining data. Its IOI discussion is qualitative and does not reproduce the original circuit-discovery and faithfulness, completeness, or minimality evaluation.

fits_no_version.finding: Self-repair of individual attention heads' direct effects occurs across the full pretraining distribution in GPT-2 small/medium/large, Pythia and Llama-7B. It is imperfect and noisy across tokens. About 30% is attributable to the LayerNorm scale. The amount depends on ablation type: zero ablation shifts LayerNorm most and can even raise logits.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ablation-based component importance in GPT-2-family models is distorted by general self-repair, partly from LayerNorm rescaling, and the distortion depends on the ablation type used.

fits_no_version.finding: Backup Name Mover Heads perform name moving on general (non-IOI) text, suggesting Name Movers and backups respond to a shared signal rather than being distinct roles.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The IOI 'backup' heads are general name-moving heads, not IOI-specific reserves.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 235 (2024)
record.problems: The IOI evidence is qualitative, with no stated model identity, sample size, prompt details, quantitative behavior measure, or uncertainty estimate. The authors describe some of the discussion as preliminary evidence.
record.rows_left_out: General-distribution self-repair, LayerNorm, and Anti-Erasure results are not IOI circuit findings and do not bear on the listed versions.

untested.parts: How much of the logit difference the backup heads restore, consistency across IOI prompts, ablation of the Name Movers themselves on IOI prompts, and which backup heads take part.
The whole circuit and its faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
IOI circuits in other models, sizes or checkpoints.
Other circuit-finding methods recovering the circuit.
Dependence of the IOI circuit's evaluation on ablation, metric or prompt distribution.

record.verdict_notes: Peer-reviewed at ICML 2024. The paper argues that self-repair is a concern for circuit discovery but is mitigated by heavy-tailed component importance. It does not test this on the IOI circuit. The IOI evidence is thin, and the V2 support should be given low weight.

versions.untested_parts: The 26-head, 7-class circuit and its faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
The extent and consistency of the backup behavior across IOI prompts; quantitative IOI performance and detailed ablation conditions are not stated.
Other models, sizes, checkpoints, and reuse of circuit components for other tasks.
Whether other circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics recover the same IOI circuit.
Whether evaluations of the IOI circuit vary by ablation, metric, or prompt distribution, or whether that circuit explains only part of IOI.
IOI behavior across name orders, templates, or numbers of names.

rows.operation_detail: Ablation of the main Name Mover Heads; detailed ablation procedure not stated.
rows.measure: Qualitative name-moving behavior by Backup Name Mover Heads
rows.value: The authors report instances in which Backup Name Mover Heads perform name moving when the Name Mover Heads are ablated.
rows.note: The report is qualitative and refers to instances; model identity, prompt details, and the magnitude of the behavior are not stated.
rows.check: Misdescribed. The text does not report an observation under Name Mover ablation. It reports that Backup Name Movers perform name moving on a more general distribution, which shows their capability, not takeover after ablation. The ablation sentence is the authors' explanatory hypothesis ("ablating the Name Mover Heads would additionally preserve the associated signal"), not a result.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Move the residual stream read by Name Movers into the residual stream read by Backup Name Movers.

conditions.value: Residual stream transfer; authors say this is equivalent to zero ablating intervening attention heads and MLP layers

rows.measure: Qualitative name-moving behavior by Backup Name Mover Heads
rows.value: The Backup Name Mover Heads begin performing name moving after the residual-stream intervention.
rows.note: No numerical effect, model identity, or prompt-level conditions are reported.
rows.check: Qualitative only: the backup heads are said to "begin performing name moving", with no magnitude to show weaker repair. So 'partial' is unsupported and the state is observed with low evidential weight. Subject is not stated; it is presumably GPT-2 small, since that is where IOI heads are defined. The authors' acknowledgements credit others with these preliminary results.
